With the key at the 70th position, LongChat-13B (16K) reaches about **35% accuracy** in the 140-pair panel of Figure 7 (page 7). That's its lowest point in this setting.

The text layer doesn't contain this number, so I read it off the plotted figure on page 7 of the PDF:

- **Which line:** LongChat-13B (16K) is the grey dashed line ("longchat-13b-16k" in the legend), in the middle panel, "140 Key-Value Pairs (~8K tokens)" (p. 7).
- **The value:** at the 70th position its marker sits just below the 40% gridline, at about 35–36%. It is roughly 37–38% at the 1st and 35th positions, then rises to about 66% at the 105th and about 89% at the 140th (p. 7). These are estimates read from the plot, so treat them as accurate to about ±1 point.
- **Why it's this low:** the paper says LongChat-13B (16K) "exhibits a different trend in the 140 key-value setting" (p. 6). When the relevant key is near the start of the context, the model "tends to generate code to retrieve the key" instead of giving the value (p. 7). That explains its low accuracy at the early and middle positions, compared with Claude-1.3, which is near 100% everywhere (p. 6).
